provenance.subject: stale pre-authorized CLI version: the tag-history row mechanically derives the next patch and normalization CONTINUES
provenance.design_reference: docs/aben-design.md section 9, B2, and section 3's explicit CLI exception

expected.note: this must NOT reach the manifest-backed version-occupied stop. Section 3 states these are different rows of the same table: aw-cli's next version is mechanically derived from tag history plus content diff, so an occupied lower intent re-derives the next free patch. A fixture that produces version-occupied here has exercised the wrong row.

aw-cli.anchor_versions.1.34.4.why_the_predecessor_is_in_the_row: aw-cli derives its next version from TAG HISTORY, so the history below the candidate is not decoration - it is the input the derivation reads. Recording 1.34.5 alone made the row's world one in which no CLI had ever shipped, which is not the state this row reconstructs and not a state the derivation can answer from. It also left the control (which removes 1.34.5) with no world at all; see that fixture's own note.
aw-cli.anchor_versions.1.34.4.predecessor_check: aw-v1.34.4 is the aw-v tag immediately below aw-v1.34.5 in version order (git tag --sort=v:refname: 1.34.3, 1.34.4, 1.34.5 - nothing between), and its commit is an ancestor of aw-v1.34.5's (git merge-base --is-ancestor, exit 0). Established from the tags themselves; the design document does not mention 1.34.4, so no record was available to copy and none is cited.

aw-cli.members.github:awebai/aw:release..warning: carries the same unverified cross-repository binding as the 1.34.5 entry below, for the same reason and with the same remedy - the external awebai/aw Release object was not queried in this authoring pass.

aw-cli.members.npm:*.occupied.1.34.4.control: the same probe against 1.34.999 returned HTTP 404 in the same run, so the 200 reports presence rather than a registry that answers 200 for any path
aw-cli.members.npm:*.occupied.1.34.4.evidence_is_weaker_than_it_looks: SEVEN npm occupancies are recorded at this version and ONE was probed. The other six rest on the composite-unit contract - that the aw CLI's platform packages publish together - not on observation. If that contract is ever false, six of these values are wrong and nothing in this fixture would show it.
aw-cli.members.npm:*.occupied.1.34.4.note: identity is null by kind, exactly as for 1.34.5 below. Recorded this way to match how the 1.34.5 row was already recorded: probing one version per-package and the other on the contract would put a second difference into a pair whose whole point is having one.

aw-cli.anchor_versions.1.34.5.note: the design states this same SHA with provenance 'the cycle record, verified 2026-08-13'. It is re-derived here from the tag itself rather than copied from that record, so the two agree by independent measurement. This is the one value in the row where a transcription error would have been invisible.

aw-cli.members.github:awebai/aw:release..source: the peeled commit of aw-v1.34.5 in the aweb repository
aw-cli.members.github:awebai/aw:release..warning: the external awebai/aw repository's Release object was not queried in this authoring pass. The design's cross-repository binding is executable (peel both tags, compare the external tree excluding .github against the cli/go subtree via the sync workflow's own ls-files -s transform); R6 should run that binding rather than trusting this identity. Not null: github releases DO expose a source identity.

aw-cli.members.npm:*.occupied.1.34.5.evidence_is_weaker_than_it_looks: SEVEN npm occupancies are recorded at this version and ONE was probed. The other six rest on the composite-unit contract - that the aw CLI's platform packages publish together - not on observation. If that contract is ever false, six of these values are wrong and nothing in this fixture would show it.
aw-cli.members.npm:*.occupied.1.34.5.note: identity is null for every npm member BY KIND, not by failure to observe: npm listings expose no source identity. This null is load-bearing - it drives provisional-by-occupancy recoverability, decided authoritatively by the staged-byte comparison at publication. Never replace it with a SHA.

current_world_note.fact: @awebai/aw 1.34.6 is ALSO present on npm today (HTTP 200), and aw-v1.34.6 resolves to e5524b4b68828154446300ea9a79a5adce8a666f
current_world_note.why_it_is_not_in_the_fixture: B2 reconstructs the state BEFORE 1.34.6 existed - that is the whole point of the row. Today's world is recorded here so a later reader who re-observes npm does not conclude the fixture is stale and 'correct' it. The fixture is historical by design.
